primary_sources: Twenty-sixth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, ratified July 1, 1971

source: original; stimulus quotes the Twenty-sixth Amendment (public domain) with an original account drawn from the grounding books

stimulus.source_note: Twenty-sixth Amendment, Section 1 (public domain). Dates and ratification speed verified against Britannica, Smithsonian Magazine, and the National Archives.
stimulus.text:
Section 1 of the Twenty-sixth Amendment to the Constitution, ratified July 1, 1971: ‘The right of citizens of the United States, who are eighteen years of age or older, to vote shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of age.’

In most states, the voting age had been 21, while young men could be drafted into the armed forces at 18. During the Vietnam War, the argument spread that anyone old enough to fight was old enough to vote. Congress proposed the amendment on March 23, 1971, and the states ratified it in about three months, the fastest ratification of any amendment.

stem: The Twenty-sixth Amendment was ratified in about three months, the fastest of any amendment. That speed best shows which of the following?

options.text: The draft-age argument had broad support across the country
Most states opposed lowering the voting age to eighteen
options.misconception: Background: Thirty-eight states ratified in about three months.

options.text: Young people had little interest in voting
options.misconception: Background: Young activists had campaigned for years to lower the voting age.

options.text: Congress passed the amendment without any debate
options.misconception: Background: The Senate voted 94 to 0 after debate.

rationales.A: Background: Thirty-eight states had to ratify, and they did so in about three months. That speed takes agreement across the country, not a narrow win.
rationales.B: Background: Thirty-eight states ratified in about three months, the opposite of broad opposition.
rationales.C: Background: Young activists had campaigned for years to lower the voting age. The speed came from their work and wide support, not from indifference.
rationales.D: Background: Congress debated the amendment in 1971, and the Senate vote was 94 to 0. Debate happened; it ended in agreement.
rationales.general:
1. Background: Ratification takes three-fourths of the states: 38 of 50.
2. The states did it in about three months, faster than any amendment before.
3. Background: That speed takes agreement across the country, including from older voters and both parties.
4. A fast ratification is a sign of broad support, not of a close fight.
Remember: Speed in ratification measures agreement: the faster it passes, the wider the support.
